'''Weston James Sandle''' {{post-nominals|country=NZL|ONZM|FRSNZ|size=85%}} (19 March 1935 – 19 February 2020) was a New Zealand physicist who specialised in the study of [[laser]]s. He was a professor at the [[University of Otago]].

==Biography==
Born in [[Christchurch]] on 19 March 1935,<ref name="Death notice"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bdmhistoricalrecords.dia.govt.nz/search/search?path=%2FqueryEntry.m%3Ftype%3Ddeaths |title=Death search: registration number 2020/5806 |website=Births, deaths & marriages online |publisher=Department of Internal Affairs |accessdate=5 March 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url= https://paperspast.natlib.govt.nz/newspapers/CHP19350321.2.2.1 |title=Births |date=21 March 1935 |work=[[The Press]] |volume=71 |issue=21428 |page=1 |access-date=21 February 2025 |via=[[PapersPast]]}}</ref> Sandle was educated at [[Christchurch Boys' High School]], and went on to study at [[University of Canterbury|Canterbury University College]], graduating [[Master of Science]] with first-class honours in mathematics in 1958.<ref name="Press 10 Jun 1958">{{cite news |url=https://paperspast.natlib.govt.nz/newspapers/CHP19580610.2.170 |title=Post-graduate fellowship |date=10 June 1958 |work=[[The Press]] |volume=97 |issue=28608 |page=18 |access-date=21 February 2025 |via=[[PapersPast]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://shadowsoftime.co.nz/university21.html |title=NZ university graduates 1870–1961: Sa–Sk |website=Shadows of Time |accessdate=23 February 2020}}</ref> He was awarded a King George VI Memorial Fellowship by the [[English-Speaking Union|English Speaking Union of the Commonwealth]] to study at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], where he earned a [[Master of Arts]] degree, and then a [[PhD]] in physics in 1968.<ref name="Press 10 Jun 1958"/><ref name="Otago Calendar">{{cite book |chapter=Emeritus Professors |title=University of Otago Calendar for 2014 |chapter-url=https://www.otago.ac.nz/study/otago064092.pdf |accessdate=23 February 2020 |year=2014 |publisher=University of Otago |location=Dunedin |page=141}}</ref><ref name="PhD">{{cite thesis |url=http://oskicat.berkeley.edu/record=b14427760~S1 |title=<sup>19</sup>F nuclear magnetic resonance in the canted antiferromagnet KMnF<sub>3</sub> |year=1968 |type=PhD |publisher=University of California}}</ref> The title of his doctoral thesis was ''<sup>19</sup>F nuclear magnetic resonance in the canted antiferromagnet KMnF<sub>3</sub>''.<ref name="PhD"/>

Appointed to the faculty of the University of Otago in 1963, Sandle rose to become a full professor in 1986.<ref name="Otago Calendar"/> He served as head of the Department of Physics at Otago for a time, and retired in 2001, when he was accorded the title of professor emeritus.<ref name="Otago Calendar"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.otago.ac.nz/otago000769.pdf |title=Vice-chancellor's review |year=2001 |publisher=University of Otago |accessdate=23 February 2020}}</ref> Much of Sandle's research was concerned with laser theory and the application of lasers, including laser stability, [[Raman laser]]s, and [[Optical cavity|laser cavity resonators]]. He was also interested in [[optical switch]]es, [[optical pumping]], [[optical bistability]] and [[optical chaos]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/37372643700 |title=W. Sandle |website=IEEE Xplore |accessdate=23 February 2020}}</ref>

In 1998, Sandle was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of New Zealand]], and he was also a Fellow of the New Zealand Institute of Physics.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/who-we-are/our-people/our-fellows/all-fellows/s-u/ |title=List of all Fellows with surnames S–U  |publisher=Royal Society Te Apārangi |accessdate=23 February 2020}}</ref> In the [[2004 New Year Honours (New Zealand)|2004 New Year Honours]], he was appointed an [[Officer of the New Zealand Order of Merit]], for services to science.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://dpmc.govt.nz/publications/new-year-honours-list-2004 |title=New Year honours list 2004 |date=31 December 2003 |publisher=Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet |accessdate=23 February 2020}}</ref>

Sandle was predeceased by his wife, Pat, to whom he was married for 56 years, in 2019.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tributes.co.nz/ViewMyTribute.aspx?id=14610 |title=In memory of Patricia Ann Sandle |website=Tributes Online |accessdate=23 February 2020}}</ref> He died in [[Dunedin]] on 19 February 2020.<ref name="Death notice">{{cite news |url=https://deaths.dompost.co.nz/obituaries/dominion-post-nz/obituary.aspx?n=weston-sandle&pid=195471924 |title=Wes Sandle death notice |date=21 February 2020 |work=Dominion Post |accessdate=23 February 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Pioneer put intellectual energies into physics|url=https://www.odt.co.nz/news/dunedin/pioneer-put-intellectual-energies-physics|last=|first=|date=2020-05-23|website=[[Otago Daily Times]] |language=en|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200523061124/https://www.odt.co.nz/news/dunedin/pioneer-put-intellectual-energies-physics|archive-date=2020-05-23|access-date=2020-05-23}}</ref>
